claims.text: The initial material is an undoped MoNbTaW-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
The undoped MoNbTaW-based alloy maintains mechanical integrity under plasma-facing conditions.
Adding approximately 5 at% Cu during melting will produce copper-enriched precipitates.
The copper-enriched precipitates will form preferentially at grain boundaries.
The copper-enriched grain-boundary precipitates will be coherent with the HEA matrix.
Copper has high intrinsic electronic thermal conductivity.
The copper-enriched precipitates will form interconnected heat-conduction pathways.
The interconnected precipitate pathways will enhance electron-driven thermal transport.
Approximately 5 at% Cu will increase the alloy's overall thermal conductivity by more than 20% relative to undoped MoNbTaW.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will help preserve mechanical integrity under loading.
The Cu-modified alloy will retain yield strength comparable to current performance standards.
The Cu-modified alloy will retain resistance to cyclic loading comparable to current performance standards.
The predicted thermal and mechanical performance will hold from 400 °C to 600 °C under steady-state plasma-facing exposure and cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
Processing variations or deviations from approximately 5 at% Cu may cause incoherent copper segregation.
Incoherent copper segregation may cause embrittlement or reduced mechanical performance.
